title.narrative: Strengthening Monitoring and Evaluation in Brazil

description.narrative: Soound monitoring and evaluation of programs and policies at the country level is critical to demonstrate progress in achieving outcomes and impact. The Government of Brazil recognizes this need and has been working to strengthen its M&E systems at the federal level in order to improve the quality of decision making and resource allocation. The GoB has requested World Bank assistance to strengthen its capacity for the design of an integratedcomma results-based M& E system. The grant will support the following activites: a) development of a collective vision for making M&E more effective in Brazil; b) institutional assessments of M& E systems in selected line ministries; c) capacity building of M&E units; and d) capacity building in impact evaluation methodology. Sound monitoring and evaluation (M&E) of programs and policies at the country level is critical to demonstrate progress in achieving outcomes and impact. The Government of Brazil recognizes this needcomma and has been working to strengthen its country systems for M&E at the federal level in order to improve the quality of decision making and resource allocation; howevercomma institutional challenges remain. In Brazilcomma the responsibilities for Monitoring and Evaluation are dispersed amongst several actorscomma and a high degree of interministerial cooperation is necessary to make the system function. Central to moving forward the M&E agenda are actors from both the executive and legislative branches of governmentcomma which include: (a) the Ministry of Planning (MoP) and the Technical Committee for M&E (CTMA)comma which supports the Inter-Ministerial Commission for M&E (CMA ) charged with developing government- wide M&E norms and policies; (b) the Federal Court of Accounts (Tribunal das Contas da Uniaocomma TCU) associated with the legislative branch of government; (c) the Secretariat of Monitoring and Articulation (Casa Civil) directly linked to the presidency; and (d) specific line ministries (e.g.comma Ministry for Social Development and Combating Hunger). In this contextcomma the Government of Brazil (GOB) has requested World Bank support to strengthen its capacity for the design and building of an integrated results-based M&E system. The GOB has requested that the grant support the Federal Court of Accounts (Tribunal das Contas da Uniaocomma TCU) associated with the legislative branch of government legislative (TCU) branch. The activities to be supported by the grant (outlined in greater detail below) would encompass the capacity building of TCU in Impact Evaluation (IE) methodology. These tasks would lay the foundation for the design of an improved results-based M&E systemcomma with an emphasis on building a coherent strategy that links performance measurement to budget and line making decision-makingcomma thus promoting accountabilitycomma efficiencycomma efficacycomma and effectiveness of government policies and programs.
